1	"""Fetch and parse LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING rows from GitHub CI run logs.
     2	
     3	Uses ``gh.run_log_read`` and ``gh.run_list_successful`` from the existing
     4	gh.py library.  Exposes three public helpers:
     5	
     6	- ``fetch_timing_rows`` — download log data for the last N successful CI runs
     7	- ``compute_medians``   — {target: median_seconds} across all rows
     8	- ``median_shard_totals`` — {shard: median_total_seconds} across all runs
     9	"""
    10	
    11	from __future__ import annotations
    12	
    13	import re
    14	import statistics
    15	from dataclasses import dataclass
    16	from collections.abc import Sequence
    17	
    18	import gh
    19	from proc import Runner
    20	
    21	
    22	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    23	class TimingRow:
    24	    run_id: int
    25	    shard: int
    26	    target: str
    27	    seconds: float
    28	
    29	
    30	_JOB_SLICE_RE = re.compile(r"test-harnesses \((\d+)\)")
    31	_TIMING_SENTINEL = "LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING\t"
    32	_SECONDS_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)s$")
    33	
    34	
    35	def fetch_timing_rows(
    36	    runner: Runner,
    37	    *,
    38	    n_runs: int = 5,
    39	    workflow: str = "ci.yaml",
    40	    branch: str = "main",
    41	    repo: str,
    42	) -> list[TimingRow]:
    43	    """Fetch LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING rows from the last *n_runs* successful CI runs.
    44	
    45	    Downloads ``gh run view --log`` for each run and parses every
    46	    ``LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING`` sentinel line emitted by ``python3 python/cli.py timing harness-mark``.
    47	    Returns an empty list (not an exception) when a run's log cannot be
    48	    fetched so a single transient failure does not abort the whole pass.
    49	    """
    50	    runs = gh.run_list_successful(
    51	        runner, repo=repo, branch=branch, workflow=workflow, limit=n_runs
    52	    )
    53	    rows: list[TimingRow] = []
    54	    for run in runs:
    55	        result = gh.run_log_read(runner, run.database_id, repo=repo)
    56	        if result.returncode != 0:
    57	            continue
    58	        rows.extend(parse_log(result.stdout, run.database_id))
    59	    return rows
    60	
    61	
    62	def parse_log(log: str, run_id: int) -> list[TimingRow]:
    63	    r"""Parse ``LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING`` sentinel lines from a combined ``gh run --log`` blob.
    64	
    65	    The combined log format from GitHub CLI is::
    66	
    67	        <job_name>\t<step_name>\t[<timestamp> ]<log_content>
    68	
    69	    ``python3 python/cli.py timing harness-mark`` emits::
    70	
    71	        LARCH_HARNESS_TIMING\t<test-name>\t<N.NNs>
    72	
    73	    so the timing tokens appear somewhere after the second tab, possibly
    74	    preceded by a timestamp.  We search for the sentinel substring rather
    75	    than relying on a fixed column count so the parser is robust to format
    76	    variations.
    77	    """
    78	    rows: list[TimingRow] = []
    79	    for line in log.splitlines():
    80	        idx = line.find(_TIMING_SENTINEL)
    81	        if idx == -1:
    82	            continue
    83	
    84	        # Job name is everything before the first tab
    85	        first_tab = line.find("\t")
    86	        job_name = line[:first_tab] if first_tab >= 0 else ""
    87	        shard_m = _JOB_SLICE_RE.search(job_name)
    88	        if not shard_m:
    89	            continue
    90	        shard = int(shard_m.group(1))
    91	
    92	        # Parse target and seconds from after the sentinel
    93	        rest = line[idx + len(_TIMING_SENTINEL):]
    94	        rest_parts = rest.split("\t", 1)
    95	        if len(rest_parts) < 2:  # noqa: PLR2004
    96	            continue
    97	        target = rest_parts[0].strip()
    98	        seconds_raw = rest_parts[1].strip()
    99	        seconds_m = _SECONDS_RE.match(seconds_raw)
   100	        if not seconds_m:
   101	            continue
   102	
   103	        rows.append(
   104	            TimingRow(
   105	                run_id=run_id,
   106	                shard=shard,
   107	                target=target,
   108	                seconds=float(seconds_m.group(1)),
   109	            )
   110	        )
   111	    return rows
   112	
   113	
   114	def compute_medians(rows: Sequence[TimingRow]) -> dict[str, float]:
   115	    """Return ``{target: median_seconds}`` across all timing rows."""
   116	    by_target: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
   117	    for row in rows:
   118	        by_target.setdefault(row.target, []).append(row.seconds)
   119	    return {t: statistics.median(times) for t, times in by_target.items()}

   122	def _split_shard_attempts(shard_rows: Sequence[TimingRow]) -> list[list[TimingRow]]:
   123	    """Split ordered rows for one ``(run_id, shard)`` into job attempts.
   124	
   125	    Multi-bash Makefile targets emit consecutive rows with the same target
   126	    label.  A retried matrix job replays the shard from the first target, so a
   127	    non-consecutive repeat of the opening target starts a new attempt.
   128	    """
   129	    if not shard_rows:
   130	        return []
   131	    attempts: list[list[TimingRow]] = [[shard_rows[0]]]
   132	    first_target = shard_rows[0].target
   133	    for row in shard_rows[1:]:
   134	        prev = attempts[-1][-1]
   135	        if row.target == prev.target:

    28	def read_shard_env(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    29	    """Parse the shard assignment from ``environ``.

    32	    when neither is set (run the full suite). Raises ``ValueError`` when only
    33	    one is set or a value is non-numeric or out of range.
    34	    """

    36	    raw_count = environ.get(ENV_SHARD_COUNT)
    37	    if raw_id is None and raw_count is None:
    38	        return None
    39	    if raw_id is None or raw_count is None:
    40	        raise ValueError(
    41	            f"{ENV_SHARD_ID} and {ENV_SHARD_COUNT} must both be set or both be unset"

    44	    shard_id = int(raw_id)

    53	
    54	def select_shard_indices(num_items: int, shard_id: int, shard_count: int) -> set[int]:

    56	
    57	    Round-robin: collected item ``i`` belongs to shard ``(i % shard_count) + 1``.
    58	    """
    59	    return {i for i in range(num_items) if i % shard_count == shard_id - 1}

   308	    """Return ``{shard: median real CI wall-clock seconds}`` across *run_ids*.

   323	                file=sys.stderr,

    46	
    47	`make test-harnesses` remains the local umbrella target and runs every regression harness wired into the `test-harnesses-N` shards plus the partition guard (`make test-harness-shards-coverage` reports the active inventory; the `Makefile` is the source of truth).     48	
    49	The shard lists live directly in `Makefile`. Rebalances use measured per-harness wall-clock times, but the checked-in layout is a **hybrid**, not a single global LPT minimax pass across all twenty shards: the slowest harnesses are pinned to shards 1–4 from observed CI (or local) timings, then the remainder are greedy-packed into shards 5–20 by **equal harness count** with an LPT-style tie-break only when choosing among bins that already have the same number of harnesses — so slow tail harnesses can still co-locate on one mid shard, and wall time is not guaranteed to match a full per-harness LPT optimum. The authoritative narrative is the `test-harnesses:` comment block in `Makefile`. New harnesses must be assigned to exactly one `test-harnesses-N:` prerequisite list; `make test-harness-shards-coverage` checks for missing, orphaned, duplicated, wrapped, or non-standard harness entries. The matrix uses `fail-fast: false`, so all twenty shards finish even after one fails. This spends more CI minutes but preserves complete diagnostics.
